findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is readable by anyone with DescribeInstanceAttribute permissions and is stored in the instance metadata and Terraform state.
The instance does not define a metadata_options block requiring IMDSv2 (http_tokens = required), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled and vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft.
The EBS volume does not enable encryption (encrypted attribute is commented out), leaving data at rest unprotected.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, exposing data at rest in the snapshot.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from the entire internet.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration path and no control over egress destinations.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IP addresses, increasing exposure to the internet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, leaving flow log data potentially exposed and unencrypted at rest.
